evidence: Receiving online DO2 sensor, t=48.0–52.0 h: values fall from ~2.48 to a minimum of 1.54 mg/L, with 8 of 21 readings below the 2.0 mg/L hard limit
Source batches at identical clock times maintained DO ~8.2–10.5 mg/L, showing receiving-transfer undercapacity rather than normal behavior
Allowed action vectors: increase_air [1.0, 1.15] vs combined [0.8, 1.15] vs strong_feed_reduction [0.6, 1.15]
Linear feasibility estimate: increase_air alone → min DO ≈ 1.78 mg/L (infeasible); combined → min DO ≈ 2.22 mg/L (feasible)
Receiving assay P: 0.0 (t=59h), 0.0 (t=119h), 0.0 (t=179h), 1.18 (t=179h) g/L — production underway and worth retaining
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 has dropped sharply since t≈48 h to 1.5–2.6 mg/L, repeatedly below the 2.0 mg/L hard limit (min observed 1.54 mg/L), while source batches at comparable times held ~8–10 mg/L — indicating a receiving-process oxygen transfer deficit, not normal behavior. A 15% aeration increase alone is insufficient: scaling observed DO by 1.15 still leaves the observed minima (~1.78 mg/L) below 2.0, so increase_air is predicted infeasible. The combined action (0.8 feed, 1.15 air) cuts oxygen demand 20% while boosting transfer 15%, moving the predicted minimum to ≈2.2 mg/L with margin against sensor noise/model mismatch. Strong feed reduction (0.6) would add margin but sacrifices more product mass (assays show product accumulating: 0 → 1.18 → 3.08 g/L), so combined is the least product-sacrificing plan that is supported to meet the constraint. Stop is unnecessary because a feasible operating plan exists.
args.uncertainty: The 0.8/1.15 multiplicative estimate is a rough linearization; true OUR response to feed reduction may be nonlinear and air-transfer gains may saturate or lag, so the ~2.2 mg/L margin could shrink. DO near-limit dynamics under KEEP may worsen before the intervention takes effect. Sensor noise (~±0.3 mg/L apparent) leaves residual risk of intermittent sub-2.0 readings; monitoring after implementation is warranted. No physical safety guarantee is established.
